notes: This page is manuscript p. 67, with a separate light pencil 135 at the foot. The author draws (224), says its vertical arrows are étales and its second horizontal arrow is an immersion locale, and then writes a small equality numbered (225). The cancelled codimension tail leaves the first d-zero live on the line; its meaning has not been repaired. The bracketed paragraph uses the word typique, a brace expression and the word cartésien; cancelled wording and two inserted groups remain distinguishable. Its raised equality is read as si d-prime-zero equals d-one, as source wording only. The rotated NB supplies a six-object diagram with a tilded subscript, a fini étale arrow label and an interior cart label. The lower morphism also bears (225); the duplicate number is preserved. The Attention paragraph says on a mis un star en exposant and writes non followed by a colon before the second D object. The final lines introduce Theta notation and the quoted phrase squelette de dim p, ending at on pose. These are records of the page’s written assertions and notation, not proof checks. The source has unresolved overdrawn letters, an additional brace-like mark, cancelled words and incomplete arrowheads; all remain flagged. The inserted contraction was given one tighter crop before resolution because the first revision crop clipped its raised t; it remains uncertain after the complete crop. All second-reading kinds use neutral spatial scope only, and the rotated marginal target is scoped separately from crossing upright body ink.

Upper lower-right exponent: the star-like group is blackened/cancelled and remains doubtful; its neighbouring high prime belongs to the subscript. Codimension tail: the strike begins after the first d_0, so that first object remains live; candidate minus, d-prime-zero, point and On a are within the cancellation, with the minus and wording unresolved. root_adjudication: Root personally inspected the complete page and all nine saved crops. Approved the visible live initial d_0, non followed by a colon, written index separators, and marginal diagram objects. The overwritten scalar, old diagram-label digit, crossed phrases, short insertion and shaft endpoints remain documented as uncertain. The unknown prior numeral beneath final4 is represented as a deleted unsure question mark, an editorial unreadable-glyph indicator, rather than an illegible-word count. Diagram labels are beside their diagrams.
legibility: The main prose is readable in most places; overwrite layers, crossed words, contracted superscript abbreviations, and the small shaft endpoints are the least secure. The rotated marginal diagram is legible enough to preserve its six objects and connections, while one lower connector endpoint remains doubtful.
